claim: The ego-motion correction is geometrically meaningful because stationary/background residual motion decreases after correction in both held-out TestReal and TrainReal.
basis: Median residual: TestReal 0.7055 px -> 0.2033 px; TrainReal 1.2008 px -> 0.7540 px.

claim: Residual suppression is not uniform across sequences/splits.
basis: Median residual reduction is 46.85% on TestReal but only 7.48% on TrainReal; difficult sequences remain.

claim: Using camera-corrected trajectories substantially improves forecasting error relative to raw image-plane trajectories for Stationary and Constant-Velocity baselines at both 2s and 5s horizons.
basis: Mean ADE reductions span 50.62% to 74.10%; mean FDE reductions span 40.73% to 74.66%.

claim: For the Constant-Velocity warning experiment, ego-motion correction improves warning discrimination and reduces false warnings at both horizons.
For Constant Velocity, corrected trajectories reduce TTE error at both horizons.
basis: TTE MAE reduction: 38.92% at 2s and 33.58% at 5s.

claim: Raw image-plane coordinates can distort the binary crossing target relative to the corrected reference representation.
basis: Raw-vs-corrected truth-label disagreement is 8.58% at 2s and 12.45% at 5s.

claim: The corrected Stationary warning rule is operationally better because its false-warning rate becomes zero.
basis: Corrected Stationary recall also becomes zero at both horizons; precision/F1/TTE are undefined because it produces no positive warnings.

claim: Ego-motion correction perfectly removes camera motion.
basis: Corrected stationary residuals remain non-zero and suppression varies substantially across splits/sequences.

claim: The manuscript should call the corrected trajectory a camera-corrected estimated reference-frame trajectory, not world-coordinate ground truth.
basis: Correction reduces apparent camera motion but does not establish metric world-space ground truth.

claim: Raw-vs-corrected results are an ego-motion ablation and should not replace the frozen primary forecasting benchmark.
basis: The ablation isolates representation/camera-motion effects; model-comparison claims remain governed by the frozen fair benchmark.
